tools.name: Grammarly
tools.desc: Improve your writing with AI-powered grammar and spell-checking
pros: Ready to use out of the box, no local install or maintenance
Free tier available, try before you upgrade
cons: Advanced features and higher limits usually require a paid plan
Requires internet connection, unusable offline
usage:
Step: Open the official site and sign up
Click the red "Visit official site" button to open the Grammarly homepage. Find "Sign Up" and log in with email or Google/GitHub.
Tip:
If the site won’t load, check your connection or try another browser.

Step: Pick the plan that fits you
New users usually get a free trial or free quota. Start with the Free tier before upgrading.
Check:
After sign-up you should see the Dashboard home.

Step: Create your first task / project
Click "New" or "Create New" and follow the guide. Pick the first template to start.
Tip:
Don’t start with a complex request. Test with one simple sentence, e.g. "Summarize this page into 3 points".

Step: Review and save the result
When done, the tool shows the result. Export, copy the link, or save locally.
Check:
If unhappy, click "Regenerate" or tweak the prompt and try again.
tools.detail: Grammarly is an AI-powered writing assistant designed to enhance the quality of your written content. It offers comprehensive grammar and spell-checking, ensuring that your text is free from errors. Key features include sentence structure checks, punctuation accuracy, and style suggestions. Grammarly is ideal for writers, students, and professionals who want to improve their written communication. It is compatible with various platforms and devices, making it convenient for use across different writing environments. Pros: Grammarly's intuitive interface makes it easy to use, and its wide range of features helps to improve the overall quality of your writing. It also offers personalized feedback based on your writing style. Limitations: Some users may find the premium features too limited compared to other advanced writing tools, and the tool can sometimes flag common phrases as incorrect.
